clue.text: Stays will alter a waist

indicators.note: to alter something is to change it, so the letters that follow get rearranged

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's note that a corset will reshape the wearer's waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a noun for corsets, matching the waist, but it is the verb: remains, holds on.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay for something is to wait for it, so stays is a synonym of waits for.

clue.text: Cry, having very little money

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for very small
P stands for penny or pence, British money

explanation.surface: Someone weeping because they are nearly broke.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to shed tears, a direct synonym of cry.

clue.text: Unwillingly late

parts.note: read 'unwillingly' as without a will and 'late' as deceased: someone who died leaving no will

explanation.surface: Someone who turned up late against their wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' is the obituary sense, dead, and 'unwillingly' is split as un-will-ingly, having made no will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies without having made a legal will is said to die in that legal state.

clue.text: A dangerous choice for mythological sailors

definitions.text: A dangerous choice for mythological sailors

parts.words: A dangerous choice for mythological sailors
parts.note: Greek sailors such as Odysseus had to pass between two perils in a strait: a six-headed monster on a rock or a whirlpool

explanation.surface: A risky decision faced by seafarers in legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'between the devil and the deep blue sea' has a classical twin: one monster or the other whirlpool, Charybdis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey this monster on one side of the strait was one of two perils sailors had to choose between.

clue.text: Many revs make small cars go

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A motoring tip that lots of engine revolutions get little cars moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revs' looks like engine revolutions, matching the cars, but it is short for Reverends, clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergy as a body, many reverends together, are collectively called the ministry.

clue.text: Noted example of inspired lunacy?

parts.note: 'noted' means set to musical notes, and lunacy is taken literally as being moved by the moon: a famous piano piece named after moonlight

explanation.surface: A celebrated case of brilliant madness.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14 got its popular nickname from a critic who likened it to moonlight on a lake; 'lunacy' comes from Latin luna, moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's famous piano sonata, inspired (so the nickname suggests) by the moon, is a musical work with notes.

clue.text: Company floated to avoid liquidation

parts.note: a company of people and animals literally floated on water to escape being drowned in the Flood

explanation.surface: A business launched on the stock market to escape going bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floated' and 'liquidation' sound like finance, but liquidation here is death by water in the biblical Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel in Genesis carried a family and pairs of animals afloat through the Flood that destroyed everything else.

clue.text: A fascinating woman about to be detected in depravity

indicators.note: something detected in a word is found sitting inside it

parts.note: depravity is wickedness, sin
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A captivating woman is about to be caught behaving wickedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to be' reads as 'soon to be', but 'about' is the piece RE and 'to be detected in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive, alluring woman, after the Sirens of myth who lured sailors.

clue.text: Meals and beers set out for get-together

indicators.note: to set things out is to lay them in a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food and drink laid out for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get-together' looks like a noun for the party, but it is the verb: to get together again.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together again as a group is a synonym for gathering a second time.

clue.text: The Greys not involved in this military duty

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The Royal Scots Greys regiment did not take part in this army task.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots Greys were a British cavalry regiment, so 'not involved' reads as they took no part; actually 'involved' scrambles the letters of GREYS NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentry duty, the stint of guarding a post and pacing back and forth, is a soldier's task.

clue.text: Jack on the way overseas

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor
a way is a road

explanation.surface: A sailor setting out on his travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being in a foreign country, across the sea.

clue.text: It's not in one's own interest to display it

definitions.text: It's not in one's own interest to display it

parts.words: It's not in one's own interest to display it
parts.note: a quality shown by someone who acts for others rather than for themselves

explanation.surface: Advice that showing this trait does you no favours.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as cynical advice, it is really a description: the quality lies in not pursuing your own interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of concern for oneself, putting others first, is the virtue of altruism.

clue.text: Top gambling game

definitions.meaning: a spinning top with marked sides telling players to pay in or take out
the game of chance played by spinning that top

explanation.definitionFit: A put-and-take is both the six-sided spinning top and the gambling game played with it.

clue.text: Country copper with a degree

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A rural policeman who holds a university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is a Caribbean island nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Apache battle cry of soldiers falling on their enemies

definitions.meaning: the famous Apache war leader of the nineteenth century

definitions.text: battle cry of soldiers falling on their enemies
definitions.meaning: the shout made by US paratroopers jumping from aircraft, literally falling on the enemy

explanation.definitionFit: The Apache leader's name became the cry American airborne troops yell as they jump.

clue.text: Lionesses making no sound

indicators.note: making here means forming or producing, so the letters of the big cats are made into something new

explanation.surface: Big cats stalking in total silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a weak anagram signal: LIONESSES, rearranged, makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no sound is silent, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Dissipated female locked up

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
pent means penned or shut in

explanation.surface: A wild woman who has been put behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or a youth that was wasted or squandered is described as dissipated.

clue.text: Clock repair?

parts.note: 'clock' is slang for a person's face, so a repair to one is cosmetic surgery

explanation.surface: Fixing a timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'clock' means face, as in 'I clocked his clock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery to tighten the skin of the face is a kind of repair to one's looks.

clue.text: Out of work, one gets led astray

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to go astray is to wander off course, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone unemployed who has been misled into bad ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idle means being without a job or not working, the same as unemployed.

clue.text: A past love, far from extinguished

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart

explanation.surface: An old romance still burning brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire and blazing is the opposite of being put out.

clue.text: It gives one the right to enter guilty plea to charge

definitions.text: It gives one the right to enter

parts.note: admitting guilt is an admission
a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: A courtroom scene where a defendant pleads guilty to an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' and 'plea' sound criminal, but charge is a price and the plea is a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: The price paid at the door to a show or museum entitles a person to go in.

clue.text: One loses one's head when in a corner

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: Someone who panics when trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses one's head' sounds like panicking, but it beheads SINGLE. An ingle is a hearth; the chimney corner is the inglenook.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireside, and the nook beside it is a chimney corner, so it is an old word for that spot.

clue.text: Information has bearing on a hereditary factor

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A piece of data that bears on heredity.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene is the unit of heredity passed from parent to child.

clue.text: T-junction snarl-up

parts.note: an angle is the meeting point where two lines join

explanation.surface: A traffic jam at a T-junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T-junction' reads as one road term; split it into T and 'junction'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl-up is a muddle or knot, which is a synonym of a tangle.

clue.text: Made case out for literary colleges

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone argued in favour of colleges devoted to literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made case out for' reads as argued for; 'out' is the anagram signal on MADE CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is a poetic word for an academy or a seat of learning, hence learned colleges.

clue.text: Time Dean suffered loss of Faculty

indicators.note: something that has suffered has been damaged, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: The university dean had a rough period when his faculty was cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' looks like a university department next to the dean, but it is a mental faculty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is the decline of mental powers such as memory and reasoning.

clue.text: Proceeded to take legal action in extremity

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an extremity is an end
to sue is to take someone to court

explanation.surface: Someone went to court as a last resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed on or came after, the sense of proceeded as a consequence.
